title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional (SAP-C02) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: A company has 60 VPCs across 12 accounts in one Region and two on-premises data centers. VPC peering has become hard to manage, and every VPC must reach the data centers. Which design reduces operational overhead most?
options: Attach all VPCs to an AWS Transit Gateway and connect the data centers to it with Direct Connect gateway or Site-to-Site VPN attachments
Create full-mesh VPC peering and add a VPN connection from every VPC to each data center
Use AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC for all traffic to the data centers
Move every workload into a single shared VPC and delete the other accounts
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway is a regional hub that replaces a peering mesh and centralizes hybrid connectivity for all attached VPCs.
questions.distractor_summary: A full mesh plus per-VPC VPNs multiplies connections. PrivateLink exposes specific services, not general routing to on premises. Collapsing accounts removes isolation the company relies on.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: A company uses AWS Direct Connect with a single 10 Gbps connection to one Direct Connect location. Leadership wants resilience against a device or location failure for critical workloads. What should the architect recommend?
options: Add a second virtual interface on the existing connection
Increase the existing connection to 100 Gbps
Replace Direct Connect with a single Site-to-Site VPN tunnel
Add a second connection at a different Direct Connect location and use both through a Direct Connect gateway with BGP
questions.correct_rationale: AWS recommends connections at separate locations for high resiliency, so a single device or site failure does not cut connectivity.
questions.distractor_summary: A second virtual interface shares the same physical link, more bandwidth does not add redundancy, and one VPN tunnel is less resilient than redundant Direct Connect.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: Several application VPCs must reach shared services such as Active Directory and a logging cluster in a central VPC, but the application VPCs must not reach each other. The company uses Transit Gateway. How should routing be designed?
options: Put all attachments in one route table with propagation enabled for every attachment
Use security groups in the shared-services VPC to block traffic between application VPCs
Use separate Transit Gateway route tables so application attachments propagate only to the shared-services route table and route only to the shared-services VPC
Create VPC peering between each application VPC and every other application VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Segmenting with Transit Gateway route tables lets spokes reach shared services while preventing spoke-to-spoke routes.
questions.distractor_summary: A single shared route table lets every VPC reach every other, security groups in the hub cannot block traffic between other VPCs, and peering every spoke does the opposite of isolation.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: Two acquired companies use the same 10.0.0.0/16 CIDR range in their VPCs. One VPC must consume an HTTP API hosted in the other. What is the simplest way to provide access without renumbering?
options: Peer the two VPCs and add routes for 10.0.0.0/16 on both sides
Expose the API through a Network Load Balancer as an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service and create an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC
Attach both VPCs to a Transit Gateway with default routing
Use a NAT gateway in each VPC and route between their public IPs over the internet without encryption
questions.correct_rationale: PrivateLink works with overlapping CIDRs because the consumer reaches the service through an endpoint with an IP from its own range.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering and Transit Gateway routing do not work with overlapping ranges, and sending unencrypted traffic over the internet adds risk.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: Which AWS feature lets on-premises DNS servers resolve names in Route 53 private hosted zones?
options: A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint
A public hosted zone with the same domain name
An internet gateway with DNS hostnames enabled
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound endpoints give on-premises resolvers IP addresses in the VPC to forward queries to Route 53 Resolver.
questions.distractor_summary: Outbound endpoints forward queries from AWS to on premises, a public zone would expose records, and an internet gateway does not provide DNS forwarding.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: Workloads in 30 VPCs must resolve an on-premises domain. The company wants to manage the forwarding rule once. What is the best approach?
options: Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and forwarding rule in a central VPC and share the rule with the other accounts through AWS RAM
Run a DNS forwarder on an EC2 instance in every VPC
Add the on-premises records to a public hosted zone
Edit the hosts file on every instance
questions.correct_rationale: Resolver rules shared through RAM let many VPCs use one central outbound endpoint and rule.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-VPC forwarders add many servers to manage, publishing internal records publicly exposes them, and hosts files do not scale.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: A company needs encrypted connectivity over its existing Direct Connect link to meet a policy that all hybrid traffic must be encrypted in transit. Which option meets this requirement?
options: Enable encryption on the private virtual interface checkbox
Use security groups to encrypt traffic
Turn on VPC Flow Logs
Run a Site-to-Site VPN over a Direct Connect public or transit virtual interface, or use MACsec on supported dedicated connections
questions.correct_rationale: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted by default, so IPsec VPN over Direct Connect or MACsec on supported links adds encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: There is no such checkbox on a private VIF, security groups do not encrypt, and flow logs only record metadata.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: A global company wants users in Asia and Europe to reach a TCP-based application in us-east-1 with lower latency and fast failover to a standby Region. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon CloudFront with caching disabled for TCP traffic
Route 53 simple routing with a long TTL
AWS Global Accelerator with endpoints in both Regions
VPC peering between the Regions
questions.correct_rationale: Global Accelerator routes TCP traffic over the AWS backbone through anycast IPs and fails over quickly between endpoint groups.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudFront handles HTTP(S), long-TTL simple routing fails over slowly, and peering does not optimize user traffic.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a Direct Connect gateway?
options: To encrypt traffic between two VPCs in the same Region
To provide internet access to private subnets
To connect Direct Connect virtual interfaces to VPCs or Transit Gateways in multiple Regions
To replace Route 53 for hybrid DNS
questions.correct_rationale: A Direct Connect gateway lets one connection reach VPCs or Transit Gateways across Regions.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt traffic, provide internet access, or handle DNS.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: Hundreds of VPCs need centralized outbound internet access through inspection appliances. Which design is commonly used?
options: An internet gateway and NAT gateway in every VPC with no inspection
A centralized egress VPC attached to Transit Gateway with NAT gateways and AWS Network Firewall or Gateway Load Balancer appliances
VPC peering from each VPC to an inspection VPC with transitive routing
Direct Connect public virtual interfaces from each VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Routing egress through a central VPC via Transit Gateway allows shared NAT and inspection.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-VPC egress skips inspection, peering is not transitive, and VPCs cannot each have Direct Connect public VIFs in that way.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: A company with 200 accounts wants to prevent anyone, including account administrators, from leaving AWS Organizations or disabling AWS CloudTrail. What should the architect use?
options: Service control policies attached at the root or OU that deny those actions
IAM permission boundaries on each administrator
AWS Config rules that alert after the change
AWS Trusted Advisor checks
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs set maximum permissions for every principal in member accounts, including administrators.
questions.distractor_summary: Boundaries must be applied per principal and can be removed by admins, Config only detects after the fact, and Trusted Advisor does not enforce.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: A central security team wants all Amazon GuardDuty findings from every account and Region in one place, with new accounts enabled automatically. What should it do?
options: Enable GuardDuty manually in each account and email findings weekly
Use CloudTrail Lake to replace GuardDuty
Enable GuardDuty only in the management account
Designate a delegated administrator account for GuardDuty in AWS Organizations and enable auto-enable for new accounts in every Region
questions.correct_rationale: Delegated administration with auto-enable centralizes findings and covers new accounts; GuardDuty is Regional, so this is done per Region.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual setup misses new accounts, CloudTrail Lake is not threat detection, and the management account alone does not cover members.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: Developers in member accounts need to create IAM roles for their applications, but must never create roles more powerful than an approved maximum. What should be enforced?
options: Give developers AdministratorAccess and review roles monthly
Block all IAM role creation for developers
Use AWS Budgets to limit role creation
Require permissions boundaries on roles they create, enforced with an IAM policy or SCP condition
questions.correct_rationale: Permissions boundaries cap the effective permissions of roles, and a condition can require the boundary on creation.
questions.distractor_summary: Monthly reviews are too late, blocking creation stops delivery, and Budgets does not govern IAM.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: Which AWS service lets a security team share AWS resources, such as subnets or Transit Gateways, with other accounts in the organization?
options: AWS Artifact
AWS License Manager
AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM)
AWS Service Catalog
questions.correct_rationale: RAM shares supported resources across accounts or the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides reports, License Manager tracks licenses, and Service Catalog offers approved products.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: An organization needs a full audit trail of API activity in all accounts that member accounts cannot delete or change. What is the best design?
options: Create a trail in each account delivering to a bucket in that same account
Create an organization trail in CloudTrail that delivers to an S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account with restrictive bucket policies and S3 Object Lock
Rely on the 90-day CloudTrail event history
Store logs in CloudWatch Logs in each member account only
questions.correct_rationale: An organization trail captures all accounts, and a separate log archive account with Object Lock prevents tampering.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-account buckets can be changed by local admins, event history is short-term, and local log groups can be deleted.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: A company wants to stop users from launching resources in Regions it does not use. How can this be enforced across the organization?
options: An SCP that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not an approved Region, excluding required global services
A tag policy requiring a Region tag
An IAM group in each account without Region permissions
A CloudWatch alarm on EC2 launches
questions.correct_rationale: An SCP with the aws:RequestedRegion condition key blocks actions in unapproved Regions across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Tag policies standardize tags, IAM groups are per account and can be bypassed by admins, and alarms do not prevent actions.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: Security wants to allow access to a sensitive S3 bucket only from principals in the company's organization. Which bucket policy condition fits best?
options: aws:PrincipalOrgID set to the organization ID
aws:SourceIp set to the corporate IP range
s3:x-amz-acl set to private
aws:CurrentTime before a set date
questions.correct_rationale: The aws:PrincipalOrgID condition limits access to principals from accounts in the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Source IP does not identify accounts, the ACL condition controls object ACLs, and time conditions do not limit by organization.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: Which service centrally manages AWS WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections, and security group policies across accounts?
options: AWS Network Firewall alone
Amazon Inspector
AWS Audit Manager
AWS Firewall Manager
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager applies security policies consistently across accounts in an organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Network Firewall is a VPC firewall, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, and Audit Manager collects audit evidence.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: A company wants employees to sign in once with its existing identity provider and get role-based access to many AWS accounts. Which approach fits best?
options: Create IAM users with the same password in each account
Share the root user of each account with team leads
Connect the identity provider to AWS IAM Identity Center and assign permission sets to groups for each account
Use Amazon Cognito user pools for workforce access to the console
questions.correct_rationale: IAM Identity Center provides workforce single sign-on with permission sets mapped to accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Duplicate IAM users and shared root credentials are insecure, and Cognito is designed for customer identities.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: A payment platform must keep RPO under 1 second and RTO under 1 minute if an entire Region fails. Its database is Amazon Aurora MySQL. Which design fits best?
options: Take Aurora snapshots every hour and copy them to another Region
Use an Aurora global database with a secondary Region and an automated failover process, with the application stack deployed in both Regions
Use a single Aurora cluster with replicas in three Availability Zones
Use AWS Backup with daily cross-Region copies
questions.correct_rationale: Aurora global database replicates with typically sub-second lag and supports fast cross-Region failover, meeting tight RPO and RTO with a warm standby stack.
questions.distractor_summary: Hourly snapshots and daily backups miss the RPO, and a single-Region cluster does not survive a Region outage.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: An application must keep running when an Availability Zone fails. It uses EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group and an RDS MySQL database. What should be configured?
options: Place all instances in one AZ and enable detailed monitoring
Spread the Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs behind a load balancer and enable RDS Multi-AZ
Use a single larger RDS instance with automated backups
Use Spot Instances in one AZ
questions.correct_rationale: Multi-AZ compute and a Multi-AZ database let the application fail over when one AZ is lost.
questions.distractor_summary: Single-AZ placements share the same failure, and backups alone do not keep the service running.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: Which disaster recovery strategy keeps a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the production environment always running in another Region?
options: Warm standby
Backup and restore
Pilot light
Multi-site active/active
questions.correct_rationale: Warm standby runs a smaller full copy that can scale up quickly during failover.
questions.distractor_summary: Backup and restore rebuilds from backups, pilot light keeps only core components such as data running, and active/active serves traffic in both Regions.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: A company accepts an RTO of 24 hours and wants the lowest-cost disaster recovery approach for a reporting system. Which strategy fits best?
options: Multi-site active/active
Warm standby with full-size capacity
Pilot light with replicas always running at full size
Backup and restore with cross-Region copies of backups and infrastructure as code to rebuild
questions.correct_rationale: With a long RTO, restoring from backups and rebuilding with templates is cheapest.
questions.distractor_summary: The other strategies keep resources running and cost more than needed.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: A stateless web application in two Regions must route users to the healthy Region automatically. Which configuration fits best?
options: Route 53 simple routing with two IP addresses
A single Application Load Balancer spanning both Regions
Route 53 failover or latency routing with health checks on each Region's endpoint
VPC peering between Regions with static routes
questions.correct_rationale: Route 53 routing policies with health checks remove unhealthy Regions from DNS answers.
questions.distractor_summary: Simple routing does not check health, ALBs are Regional, and peering does not steer users.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: An order-processing system loses messages when a downstream service is slow. Which design change improves resilience most?
options: Increase the instance size of the upstream service
Retry requests synchronously without a limit
Place an Amazon SQS queue between the services and use a dead-letter queue for messages that repeatedly fail
Store messages in the upstream service's memory
questions.correct_rationale: A queue decouples producer and consumer, absorbs bursts, and a DLQ isolates poison messages.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger instances do not decouple, unlimited retries cause cascading load, and in-memory storage loses messages on failure.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: What does "static stability" mean in AWS resilience guidance?
options: A system never changes its configuration in production
A system keeps working during a dependency failure without needing to make changes, such as launching new capacity
A system uses only static websites
A system has the same number of instances every day
questions.correct_rationale: Statically stable designs pre-provision capacity, for example across AZs, so an impairment does not require control plane actions to recover.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not about freezing configuration, static sites, or fixed daily instance counts.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: A company needs a shared file system for Linux instances in three Availability Zones that keeps data available if one AZ fails. Which option fits best?
options: Amazon EFS with Regional (Standard) storage
An EBS volume attached to one instance in each AZ with manual copies
EFS One Zone storage
Instance store volumes
questions.correct_rationale: EFS Regional storage stores data redundantly across multiple AZs.
questions.distractor_summary: EBS copies are manual, One Zone is in a single AZ, and instance store is temporary.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company is starting a large migration and wants a well-architected multi-account environment with guardrails, account vending, and centralized logging set up quickly. What should it use?
options: Create accounts manually and configure each one by hand
Use one account with many VPCs
Use AWS Service Catalog alone without Organizations
AWS Control Tower to set up a landing zone with organizational units and controls
questions.correct_rationale: Control Tower automates landing zone setup with Organizations, guardrails, account factory, and log archive and audit accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual setup is slow and inconsistent, one account limits isolation, and Service Catalog alone does not build the landing zone.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: Why do organizations separate workloads into multiple AWS accounts?
options: Each account receives free compute credits
AWS requires one account per application
Multiple accounts remove the need for IAM
Accounts are strong security, billing, and quota boundaries, which limits the blast radius of mistakes
questions.correct_rationale: Separate accounts isolate permissions, limits, and costs between workloads and environments.
questions.distractor_summary: There are no free credits per account, it is not required, and IAM is still needed in each account.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company wants new accounts created by teams to automatically get a baseline VPC, IAM roles, and Config rules, with drift detection. Which approach fits best?
options: Email each team a checklist of resources to create
Use the management account to run scripts manually after each request
Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory with customizations, such as Account Factory Customization or Customizations for Control Tower, using CloudFormation StackSets
Rely on AWS Trusted Advisor to create the baseline
questions.correct_rationale: Account Factory with customization pipelines applies a consistent baseline to every new account.
questions.distractor_summary: Checklists and manual scripts are error prone, and Trusted Advisor does not deploy resources.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company wants a single place to deploy a CloudFormation template across all accounts in an OU, including accounts added later. What should it use?
options: A separate CloudFormation stack in each account deployed by hand
CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions and automatic deployment enabled for the OU
AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
questions.correct_rationale: Service-managed StackSets integrate with Organizations and can deploy automatically to new accounts in target OUs.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual stacks miss new accounts, Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications, and Parameter Store stores configuration values.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: In a typical AWS Control Tower landing zone, what are the log archive and audit accounts used for?
options: Centrally storing logs and giving security teams cross-account access for audits
Running production workloads
Paying for all usage in the organization
Hosting developer sandboxes
questions.correct_rationale: Control Tower creates dedicated shared accounts for log storage and security auditing.
questions.distractor_summary: Production and sandboxes live in workload accounts, and billing is handled by the management account.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company wants to restrict which AWS services developers can use in sandbox accounts while allowing everything in production accounts. How should it structure this?
options: Place sandbox accounts in a separate OU and attach an SCP that allows only approved services
Create IAM groups in production accounts only
Use one OU for all accounts and rely on naming conventions
Use AWS Budgets to block services
questions.correct_rationale: OUs let different SCPs apply to different groups of accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Production IAM groups do not affect sandboxes, naming conventions do not enforce anything, and Budgets does not block services directly.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company must allow a central networking account to own all VPCs and subnets while application teams launch resources into them from their own accounts. Which approach fits best?
options: Peer each application account VPC with the network account VPC
Give application teams IAM users in the network account
Copy the VPC configuration into each account with CloudFormation
Use VPC sharing by sharing subnets from the network account through AWS RAM
questions.correct_rationale: Shared VPCs let participants launch resources into centrally owned subnets while network control stays central.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering creates separate VPCs, users in the network account weaken account isolation, and copying VPCs does not centralize ownership.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: Which AWS Organizations feature standardizes tag keys and allowed values across accounts?
options: Backup policies
Service control policies
Tag policies
AI services opt-out policies
questions.correct_rationale: Tag policies define and help enforce consistent tags across the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Backup policies manage backups, SCPs limit permissions, and AI opt-out policies control data use by AI services.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: Finance wants to see AWS costs per business unit across 80 accounts and charge them back monthly. What is the most effective approach?
options: Ask each team to estimate its costs in a spreadsheet
Use consolidated billing with cost allocation tags or AWS Cost Categories and analyze them in Cost Explorer or the Cost and Usage Report
Create one account per invoice line item
Use AWS Pricing Calculator for actual costs
questions.correct_rationale: Tags and Cost Categories group real costs by business dimension across consolidated billing.
questions.distractor_summary: Estimates are inaccurate, account-per-item is unworkable, and the Pricing Calculator models planned costs.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company's Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts are not reaching some accounts. Which billing behavior should the architect explain?
options: Discounts only apply in the account that bought them, with no way to share
With consolidated billing, discounts are shared across accounts by default unless sharing is turned off for specific accounts
Discounts apply only to Spot Instances
Discounts apply only in the us-east-1 Region
questions.correct_rationale: Organizations shares RI and Savings Plans benefits across accounts by default, and admins can disable sharing for chosen accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Sharing is possible, discounts do not apply to Spot, and they are not limited to one Region.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company runs a steady baseline of EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage across many instance families that change often. Which commitment provides flexible savings?
options: Compute Savings Plans
Standard Reserved Instances for one instance type
Spot Instances for all workloads
Dedicated Hosts
questions.correct_rationale: Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, Regions, Fargate, and Lambda.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard RIs are tied to attributes, Spot can be interrupted, and Dedicated Hosts add cost.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: Which feature detects unusual spikes in AWS spending using machine learning and sends alerts?
options: AWS Budgets reports only
AWS Trusted Advisor service limits
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
questions.correct_rationale: Cost Anomaly Detection learns spending patterns and alerts on unexpected changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Budget reports show fixed thresholds, service limits concern quotas, and GuardDuty detects security threats.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: Teams frequently launch oversized instances. Leadership wants guardrails that stop very large instance types in non-production accounts. What fits best?
options: A monthly email reminding teams to choose small instances
An S3 lifecycle policy
An SCP on the non-production OU that denies ec2:RunInstances for disallowed instance types
AWS Artifact reports
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs can deny actions based on conditions such as ec2:InstanceType.
questions.distractor_summary: Reminders do not enforce, lifecycle policies manage objects, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company has many idle Elastic IP addresses, unattached EBS volumes, and old snapshots across accounts. Which approach finds and removes waste continuously?
options: Delete the oldest account in the organization
Increase the budget threshold
Use AWS Trusted Advisor and AWS Config rules to detect idle resources, and automate cleanup with Systems Manager Automation or Lambda
Disable consolidated billing
questions.correct_rationale: Automated detection plus automated remediation keeps waste low over time.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting accounts, raising budgets, or disabling consolidated billing do not remove waste.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: Which tool gives right-sizing recommendations for EC2 instances, EBS volumes, Lambda functions, and ECS services on Fargate?
options: AWS Artifact
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Control Tower
Amazon Athena
questions.correct_rationale: Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics and recommends optimal resource configurations.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides reports, Control Tower sets up landing zones, and Athena queries data.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company wants each application team to see only its own costs in Cost Explorer while finance sees everything. What should be set up?
options: Use AWS Billing Conductor or Cost Categories with IAM access to cost data scoped by account, or enable member account access to their own costs
Give every team access to the management account root user
Share a screenshot of the full bill
Disable Cost Explorer for all users
questions.correct_rationale: Billing tools and member-account cost visibility let teams see their own spending while finance keeps the full view.
questions.distractor_summary: Root access is unsafe, screenshots are static and overshare, and disabling Cost Explorer removes visibility.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company wants to understand data transfer costs between Availability Zones for a chatty microservice architecture. What is the most useful source?
options: The AWS Health Dashboard
IAM Access Analyzer findings
AWS Artifact SOC reports
The Cost and Usage Report filtered by usage type for regional data transfer, combined with VPC Flow Logs analysis
questions.correct_rationale: CUR exposes inter-AZ transfer charges, and flow logs show which services generate the traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: The other sources do not show data transfer costs.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: Which billing feature lets a company group accounts and charges into custom groups, such as products or environments, for reporting?
options: AWS Organizations SCPs
AWS Resource Groups only
AWS Shield Advanced
AWS Cost Categories
questions.correct_rationale: Cost Categories map costs into custom groupings using rules on accounts, tags, and services.
questions.distractor_summary: SCPs limit permissions, Resource Groups organize resources but do not create billing groups by themselves, and Shield protects against DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: A company has Transit Gateways in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. VPCs in both Regions must communicate privately. What is the simplest option?
options: Create VPN connections between every pair of VPCs
Use a single Transit Gateway shared across both Regions
Create a Transit Gateway inter-Region peering attachment and add static routes for the remote CIDRs
Use VPC sharing across Regions through AWS RAM
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway peering connects hubs across Regions over the AWS backbone, using static routes.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-pair VPNs add complexity, a Transit Gateway is a Regional resource, and VPC sharing works only within a Region.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Architect network connectivity strategies
questions.question: An application in a VPC must call a SaaS provider's service privately without traversing the internet. The provider offers an endpoint service. What should the company create?
options: A VPC peering connection to the provider's VPC
An interface VPC endpoint that connects to the provider's PrivateLink endpoint service
A NAT gateway with an Elastic IP address
A gateway endpoint for Amazon DynamoDB
questions.correct_rationale: Interface endpoints consume PrivateLink services privately inside the VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering exposes whole networks, NAT uses the internet, and gateway endpoints only exist for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: A company wants to detect and block outbound traffic from all VPCs to known malicious domains, with centrally managed rules. Which service fits best?
options: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule groups shared through Firewall Manager or AWS RAM
Security groups that list malicious IP addresses
Network ACLs with deny rules for each domain name
Amazon Inspector network reachability findings
questions.correct_rationale: DNS Firewall blocks DNS queries to listed domains, and rule groups can be applied across VPCs and accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs filter IP addresses, not domain names, and Inspector does not block traffic.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Prescribe security controls
questions.question: Auditors require that all EBS volumes in the organization are encrypted. What is the most effective preventive control?
options: Enable EBS encryption by default in every account and Region, and use an SCP that denies creating unencrypted volumes
Ask teams to tick the encryption box when creating volumes
Run a monthly script that lists unencrypted volumes
Use AWS Shield Advanced
questions.correct_rationale: Default encryption plus a deny on unencrypted creation prevents non-compliant volumes from being created.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps and monthly scripts are detective at best, and Shield protects against DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design reliable and resilient architectures
questions.question: A company wants to test how its multi-AZ application behaves when an Availability Zone becomes impaired, in a controlled way. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Config conformance packs
Amazon Macie
AWS Artifact
AWS Fault Injection Service with an AZ power interruption scenario
questions.correct_rationale: Fault Injection Service runs controlled experiments, including scenarios that simulate AZ disruptions.
questions.distractor_summary: Config checks configuration, Macie finds sensitive data, and Artifact provides reports.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Design a multi-account AWS environment
questions.question: A company wants approved product teams to deploy pre-approved architectures, such as a standard three-tier stack, in their own accounts without needing full CloudFormation permissions. What fits best?
options: Give every team AdministratorAccess
Email CloudFormation templates to teams
AWS Service Catalog portfolios shared to the organization with launch constraints
Use AWS Artifact agreements
questions.correct_rationale: Service Catalog offers governed self-service with launch roles that grant only what the product needs.
questions.distractor_summary: Admin access is too broad, emailed templates are ungoverned, and Artifact handles agreements.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Determine cost optimization and visibility strategies
questions.question: A company wants alerts when any linked account's spending grows faster than expected this month, and wants one budget to cover each business unit's accounts. What fits best?
options: One CloudWatch alarm per EC2 instance
AWS Budgets filtered by linked accounts or Cost Categories, with forecast-based alerts
AWS Trusted Advisor cost checks only
A Config rule for each account
questions.correct_rationale: Budgets can scope to groups of accounts or categories and alert on forecasted spend.
questions.distractor_summary: Instance alarms do not track total spend, Trusted Advisor gives optimization advice, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: A team wants to release a new version of an ECS service to 10 percent of traffic, watch metrics, and then shift all traffic, with automatic rollback on alarms. What should it use?
options: Update the task definition in place and restart all tasks at once
AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment for ECS with a canary traffic-shifting configuration and CloudWatch alarm rollback
Create a new cluster manually and change DNS records by hand
Use AWS Batch job queues
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy for ECS supports canary and linear traffic shifting with alarm-based rollback.
questions.distractor_summary: In-place restarts hit all users at once, manual DNS changes are slow and error prone, and Batch is for batch jobs.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: An application uses Lambda functions behind API Gateway. The team wants new versions to receive 5 percent of traffic for 15 minutes before full release. Which approach fits best?
options: Use Lambda aliases with weighted traffic shifting managed by CodeDeploy (for example Canary10Percent15Minutes or a custom configuration)
Deploy a new API Gateway stage and ask users to switch URLs
Use EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks
Update the $LATEST version directly in production
questions.correct_rationale: Aliases with weighted routing and CodeDeploy deployment preferences enable canary releases for Lambda.
questions.distractor_summary: Asking users to switch is not a controlled rollout, lifecycle hooks are for EC2, and updating $LATEST releases to everyone.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: Which deployment strategy keeps the old environment running while the new environment receives traffic, allowing instant rollback by switching back?
options: In-place rolling with no batch size
Recreate
All at once
Blue/green
questions.correct_rationale: Blue/green deploys to a separate environment and switches traffic, so rollback means switching back.
questions.distractor_summary: The other strategies replace the old version in place, so rollback requires redeploying.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: A company wants identical infrastructure deployed to development, staging, and production accounts from one template with environment-specific values. What fits best?
options: Create each environment by hand in the console
Copy production resources with snapshots only
CloudFormation or AWS CDK templates with parameters, deployed through a pipeline to each account
Use AWS Artifact to store templates
questions.correct_rationale: Parameterized infrastructure as code deployed through a pipeline keeps environments consistent.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual creation drifts, snapshots do not recreate infrastructure, and Artifact is for compliance reports.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: An enterprise wants every infrastructure change reviewed, tested, and deployed automatically across 40 accounts with approvals for production. Which architecture fits best?
options: Developers run CloudFormation from their laptops into each account
One pipeline per account with no approvals
A central CodePipeline in a tooling account using cross-account roles, with manual approval actions before production stages
Changes made directly in the console and recorded in a wiki
questions.correct_rationale: A central pipeline with cross-account roles and approvals gives consistent, auditable deployments.
questions.distractor_summary: Laptop deployments and console changes are unaudited, and pipelines without approvals bypass production control.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: A team wants to deploy a containerized web app without managing servers and with automatic HTTPS, scaling, and deployments from a container registry. Which service is simplest?
options: Amazon EC2 with a self-managed Docker host
AWS App Runner
AWS Batch
Amazon EMR
questions.correct_rationale: App Runner deploys containerized web apps from source or images with managed scaling and TLS.
questions.distractor_summary: Self-managed EC2 hosts add operations work, Batch and EMR serve batch and big data workloads.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: What is an immutable deployment?
options: Deploying new instances with the new version and replacing old instances instead of updating them in place
Deploying only on weekends
Updating code directly on running servers
Deploying without any testing
questions.correct_rationale: Immutable deployments replace infrastructure, which avoids configuration drift and simplifies rollback.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options are not immutable practices.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A company must recover an on-premises application in AWS with RPO in seconds and RTO in minutes, using block-level replication from physical and virtual servers. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Backup daily jobs
AWS DataSync scheduled tasks
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
questions.correct_rationale: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers at block level and launches recovery instances quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Daily backups miss the RPO, DataSync copies files on a schedule, and S3 replication copies objects, not servers.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A DynamoDB-backed application must be readable and writable in two Regions with automatic replication. Which feature fits best?
options: DynamoDB Streams to a Lambda function in each Region that copies data manually
Daily on-demand backups copied to another Region
DynamoDB Accelerator in each Region
DynamoDB global tables
questions.correct_rationale: Global tables replicate data across Regions with multi-active writes.
questions.distractor_summary: Custom stream copying is more work, daily backups are not live replication, and DAX is a cache.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A company stores critical objects in Amazon S3 and needs a copy in another Region within minutes, with a predictable replication time. What should be configured?
options: S3 Same-Region Replication
S3 lifecycle transitions to Glacier
S3 Cross-Region Replication with S3 Replication Time Control
S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.correct_rationale: Replication Time Control replicates most objects within seconds and provides an SLA for 99.99 percent within 15 minutes.
questions.distractor_summary: Same-Region replication stays in one Region, lifecycle rules change storage class, and Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A company uses the pilot light DR strategy. Which components should be running all the time in the recovery Region?
options: Full-size application servers serving production traffic
Core data stores with live replication, such as database replicas, while application servers are off or not yet launched
Nothing at all until a disaster occurs
Only the AWS Health Dashboard
questions.correct_rationale: Pilot light keeps critical data replicated and minimal infrastructure ready, then scales out compute during recovery.
questions.distractor_summary: Full-size serving is warm standby or active/active, and running nothing is backup and restore.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A company wants a consistent, centrally managed backup policy for EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, and EFS across all accounts with copies to a separate account. What fits best?
options: AWS Backup with organization-level backup policies and cross-account copy to a vault in a backup account
Manual snapshots in each account
AWS Config rules only
Amazon S3 versioning for databases
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Backup policies in Organizations apply consistent plans and can copy to vaults in another account.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual snapshots are inconsistent, Config only checks, and S3 versioning does not back up databases.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: What does AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode provide?
options: Write-once protection that prevents anyone, including the root user, from deleting backups before retention ends
Faster backups by compressing data
Automatic restore testing
Encryption with a customer key
questions.correct_rationale: Vault Lock in compliance mode enforces immutable retention for recovery points.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not about speed, restore testing, or key choice.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A web application must let customers sign up and sign in with social identity providers and get temporary AWS credentials to upload files to their own S3 prefix. Which approach fits best?
options: IAM users for every customer
A shared IAM access key embedded in the mobile app
AWS IAM Identity Center for customers
Amazon Cognito user pools with identity pools, using IAM policies that scope access by the user's identity
questions.correct_rationale: Cognito handles customer sign-in and federation, and identity pools issue scoped temporary credentials.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM users per customer do not scale, embedded keys leak, and Identity Center is for workforce access.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A company must encrypt data at rest in DynamoDB and S3 with keys it controls, and must be able to audit every key use. What should it use?
options: AWS owned keys only
Client-side encryption with keys stored in the application code
AWS KMS customer managed keys with CloudTrail logging of key usage
S3 bucket keys without KMS
questions.correct_rationale: Customer managed KMS keys give control over policies and rotation, and CloudTrail records each use.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS owned keys are not visible to customers, keys in code are unsafe, and bucket keys are a KMS cost optimization rather than a key choice.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: An API must be protected from SQL injection and from bots, and rate limited per client IP. It is served through CloudFront. What should be added?
options: Security groups on the origin with deny rules
AWS WAF web ACL on the CloudFront distribution with managed rule groups, Bot Control, and rate-based rules
Network ACLs on the public subnets
Amazon Inspector agent on the API servers
questions.correct_rationale: WAF inspects HTTP requests at the edge, with managed rules for injection, bot control, and rate limits.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs cannot inspect HTTP content, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities rather than filtering traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A financial application requires that database credentials be rotated every 30 days without downtime. Which approach fits best?
options: Store credentials in environment variables and update them manually
Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation and have the application retrieve them at runtime
Hard-code credentials and redeploy monthly
Store credentials in a public S3 bucket with encryption
questions.correct_rationale: Secrets Manager rotates credentials on a schedule, and applications that fetch them at runtime pick up new values.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual updates and hard-coding are error prone, and public buckets are unsafe even with encryption.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: Which service lets an application in a private subnet call AWS APIs such as Amazon SQS without internet access?
options: Interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink
An internet gateway
A public NAT gateway with no route table changes
AWS Global Accelerator
questions.correct_rationale: Interface endpoints give private connectivity to supported AWS services.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways and NAT use the internet path, and Global Accelerator speeds public traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A healthcare company must ensure that data from one tenant is never readable by another tenant in a shared DynamoDB table. Which control fits best?
options: A separate VPC per tenant
Encrypting each tenant's items with the same KMS key
Client-side filtering of query results
IAM policies using the dynamodb:LeadingKeys condition with the tenant ID from the caller's identity
questions.correct_rationale: Fine-grained access control with LeadingKeys limits each caller to items whose partition key matches its tenant.
questions.distractor_summary: VPCs do not isolate table items, one shared key does not separate tenants, and client filtering can be bypassed.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A new application expects unpredictable traffic spikes of 10 times normal load. Which design best absorbs spikes without dropping requests?
options: Size servers for average load and turn off Auto Scaling
Use one very large instance
Front the processing tier with an SQS queue and scale consumers on queue depth
Reject requests when CPU passes 50 percent
questions.correct_rationale: A queue buffers bursts while consumers scale based on backlog.
questions.distractor_summary: Average-sized fixed fleets and single instances get overwhelmed, and rejecting requests loses work.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A company needs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database that keeps serving reads during a writer failover, with failover typically under 30 seconds. What should be configured?
options: A single Aurora instance with automated backups
An RDS for PostgreSQL instance with read replicas in another Region only
An Aurora cluster with Aurora Replicas in other AZs, with applications using the cluster and reader endpoints
Aurora Serverless v2 with zero replicas
questions.correct_rationale: Aurora promotes a replica during failover, and the cluster endpoint moves to the new writer quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: A single instance must be replaced, cross-Region replicas do not give fast in-Region failover, and zero replicas means no failover target.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: What is the purpose of exponential backoff with jitter when calling AWS APIs?
options: To speed up every request
To spread out retries so clients do not overload a service with synchronized retry storms
To encrypt API calls
To reduce costs of data transfer
questions.correct_rationale: Increasing waits with randomness reduces contention and helps throttled services recover.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not speed requests, encrypt data, or reduce transfer costs.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A global user base needs a highly available, low-latency static website with HTTPS and a custom domain. Which design fits best?
options: Amazon S3 as the origin behind CloudFront with origin access control, an ACM certificate, and Route 53 alias records
A single EC2 instance in one Region with an Elastic IP
An S3 bucket with public website hosting and no CDN
An Application Load Balancer in front of S3
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFront caches globally, OAC keeps the bucket private, ACM provides TLS, and Route 53 alias records map the domain.
questions.distractor_summary: One instance is a single point of failure, a public bucket lacks HTTPS on custom domains and caching, and ALBs do not front S3 directly.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A company needs to process millions of IoT messages per hour with strict ordering per device and replay ability for 7 days. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon SQS standard queues
Amazon SNS standard topics
Amazon S3 event notifications
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with the device ID as the partition key and extended retention
questions.correct_rationale: Kinesis preserves order per shard key and supports retention and replay for days.
questions.distractor_summary: SQS standard and SNS standard do not guarantee ordering or replay, and S3 notifications are not a streaming log.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: A read-heavy product catalog on Amazon RDS shows high CPU from repeated identical queries. What improves performance most cost-effectively?
options: Move to a larger RDS instance class each month
Disable automated backups
Add more EBS volumes to the database
Add Amazon ElastiCache to cache frequent query results
questions.correct_rationale: Caching repeated reads in memory offloads the database and lowers latency.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger instances cost more without fixing the pattern, backups are not the cause, and extra volumes do not reduce CPU.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: A DynamoDB table supports a mobile game. One partition key value, used for a global leaderboard, receives most writes and causes throttling. What should the architect change?
options: Increase the table's provisioned capacity only
Switch the table to the Standard-Infrequent Access table class
Use write sharding by adding a random or calculated suffix to the hot key and aggregate results
Add a global secondary index on the same key
questions.correct_rationale: Spreading writes across several key values avoids a hot partition limit.
questions.distractor_summary: More capacity does not lift per-partition limits, the table class affects cost, and an index on the same key keeps the hot spot.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: A data analytics team runs interactive SQL on 2 PB of data with many concurrent users and needs consistent performance. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon RDS for MySQL
Amazon Redshift with concurrency scaling or Redshift Serverless
Amazon DynamoDB scans
A single EC2 instance running PostgreSQL
questions.correct_rationale: Redshift is built for large-scale analytics, and concurrency scaling adds capacity for concurrent queries.
questions.distractor_summary: OLTP databases and DynamoDB scans are not designed for petabyte analytics.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: Which EC2 feature places instances close together for the lowest network latency between them?
options: A cluster placement group
A spread placement group
A partition placement group across AZs
An Auto Scaling group across Regions
questions.correct_rationale: Cluster placement groups pack instances in one AZ for low-latency, high-throughput networking.
questions.distractor_summary: Spread and partition groups separate instances for resilience, and Auto Scaling groups are Regional.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: Users upload large files to S3 from around the world and report slow uploads. What improves upload speed with minimal change?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and use multipart upload
Move the bucket to the Region with the most users only
Use S3 One Zone-IA
Turn on S3 Object Lock
questions.correct_rationale: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through edge locations, and multipart upload sends parts in parallel.
questions.distractor_summary: Moving the bucket helps one region only, storage class and Object Lock do not affect upload speed.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A new image-processing workload runs in short bursts, can tolerate interruptions, and must be cheap. Which compute choice fits best?
options: On-Demand Dedicated Hosts
Three-year Standard Reserved Instances
Large always-on instances sized for peak
EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with diversified instance types, or AWS Batch using Spot
questions.correct_rationale: Interruptible batch work fits Spot, and diversifying instance types improves availability.
questions.distractor_summary: Dedicated Hosts and long reservations add cost or commitment, and always-on peak capacity wastes money.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: An application logs 5 TB per day to S3. Logs are queried heavily for 30 days, rarely for a year, and must be kept for 7 years. What is the most cost-effective storage plan?
options: Keep everything in S3 Standard for 7 years
Store logs on EBS volumes
Lifecycle rules: S3 Standard for 30 days, then S3 Standard-IA or Glacier Instant Retrieval, then Glacier Deep Archive until 7 years
Delete logs after 30 days
questions.correct_rationale: Tiering by age matches cost to access patterns while meeting retention.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard for 7 years is costly, EBS is expensive for logs, and deleting breaks retention.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A team plans an API with low and unpredictable traffic. Which architecture minimizes cost?
options: An always-on fleet of EC2 instances behind a load balancer
API Gateway with Lambda and DynamoDB on-demand capacity
An Amazon EMR cluster
A provisioned Redshift cluster
questions.correct_rationale: Serverless services charge per request, so idle time costs little.
questions.distractor_summary: Always-on fleets and clusters are billed even when idle.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: Which pricing option for DynamoDB is best when traffic is unpredictable or new?
options: Provisioned capacity with reserved capacity purchases
On-demand capacity mode
Provisioned capacity set to the peak forever
Standard-IA table class with fixed capacity
questions.correct_rationale: On-demand mode charges per request and scales instantly without capacity planning.
questions.distractor_summary: Reservations and fixed peak capacity suit steady predictable traffic, and table class addresses storage cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A company runs many small development databases that are idle most nights and weekends. What reduces cost most with little effort?
options: Use Aurora Serverless v2 or schedule RDS instances to stop outside working hours
Buy three-year Reserved Instances for every development database
Move databases to larger instance classes
Enable Multi-AZ on all development databases
questions.correct_rationale: Scaling down or stopping idle databases removes most of the waste.
questions.distractor_summary: Reservations commit to always-on use, larger classes cost more, and Multi-AZ doubles cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A multi-tier app sends large amounts of data between EC2 instances in different Availability Zones. How can inter-AZ data transfer costs be reduced without hurting availability much?
options: Move all instances to one AZ permanently
Route traffic through the internet
Use larger instances
Use AZ-aware routing so most calls stay within the same AZ, while keeping capacity in multiple AZs for failover
questions.correct_rationale: Keeping traffic local to an AZ cuts charges while multi-AZ capacity still covers failures.
questions.distractor_summary: A single AZ removes resilience, internet routing adds cost and risk, and instance size does not change transfer charges.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: A company deploys the same application to 15 Regions. Each Regional deployment must wait until the previous Region is healthy for one hour. What is the most maintainable approach?
options: Deploy to all Regions at the same moment
Have engineers deploy each Region manually from a checklist
A pipeline with sequential Regional stages, each with automated health checks or bake time before promotion
Deploy only to one Region and replicate the instances with snapshots
questions.correct_rationale: Staged, wave-based deployments with bake times limit the blast radius of a bad release.
questions.distractor_summary: Simultaneous deploys affect every Region at once, manual work is error prone, and snapshot copying is not a deployment process.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Design a deployment strategy to meet business requirements
questions.question: Developers want short-lived feature environments that mirror production and are destroyed automatically when a pull request closes. Which approach fits best?
options: A permanent shared test environment edited by hand
Copy production databases into each developer laptop
Infrastructure as code deployed by a pipeline triggered by pull request events, with teardown on merge or close
Ask operations to build each environment manually
questions.correct_rationale: Automated create and destroy keeps environments consistent and avoids paying for idle stacks.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared hand-edited environments drift, copying production data to laptops is a security risk, and manual builds are slow.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A stateful application on EC2 stores data on EBS. The company needs crash-consistent backups across several volumes attached to the same instance. What should it use?
options: Separate snapshots of each volume taken minutes apart
Multi-volume EBS snapshots (snapshot sets) or AWS Backup for the instance
Copying files to S3 with a cron job
EBS volume resizing
questions.correct_rationale: Multi-volume snapshots capture all volumes of an instance at the same point in time.
questions.distractor_summary: Snapshots taken at different times can be inconsistent, file copies miss in-flight data, and resizing is not a backup.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: A company's RTO is 15 minutes for a web tier in a second Region. The database replicates continuously. Which approach keeps costs low while meeting RTO?
options: Keep AMIs and infrastructure as code ready, run a minimal Auto Scaling group in the DR Region, and scale out on failover
Keep a full-size duplicate fleet running in the DR Region
Rebuild the web tier from scratch with manual steps during an outage
Rely on daily backups of the web servers
questions.correct_rationale: A small running footprint that scales out quickly meets a 15-minute RTO at lower cost than full duplication.
questions.distractor_summary: A full duplicate costs more than needed, manual rebuilds are slow, and stateless web servers do not need daily backups to recover.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Design a solution to ensure business continuity
questions.question: Which metric defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time?
options: Recovery time objective (RTO)
Mean time between failures
Service level indicator
Recovery point objective (RPO)
questions.correct_rationale: RPO is how much data, measured in time, the business can afford to lose.
questions.distractor_summary: RTO is how long recovery can take, MTBF measures reliability, and SLIs measure service behavior.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A company processes credit card data and wants to reduce PCI DSS scope for its web application. Which design choice helps most?
options: Encrypt card numbers with the same key used for all other data
Store card numbers in DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery
Log full card numbers for troubleshooting
Tokenize card data through the payment provider so card numbers never reach the company's systems
questions.correct_rationale: If card data never enters the environment, far fewer systems are in PCI scope.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared keys and storage choices keep card data in scope, and logging card numbers violates PCI requirements.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: An application on EC2 needs to read objects from an S3 bucket in another account. Security forbids long-term access keys. What should be configured?
options: An IAM user in the other account with keys stored on the instance
A public bucket policy limited by user agent string
An instance profile role with permissions to the bucket, plus a bucket policy that allows that role
S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account access works with a role on the instance and a bucket policy that names it.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored keys break the requirement, user agent conditions are trivially spoofed, and Transfer Acceleration is about speed.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: A company needs to inspect traffic between VPCs and to the internet with stateful rules and intrusion prevention, managed as an AWS service. Which service fits best?
options: Security groups only
AWS Network Firewall in an inspection VPC attached to Transit Gateway
Network ACLs only
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.correct_rationale: Network Firewall provides stateful inspection and IPS rules as a managed service.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs do not inspect payloads, and GuardDuty detects threats but does not filter traffic inline.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Determine security controls based on requirements
questions.question: What does an S3 VPC endpoint policy allow you to do?
options: Restrict which buckets and actions can be reached through that endpoint
Encrypt all objects with a new key
Speed up uploads from the internet
Replicate buckets across Regions
questions.correct_rationale: Endpoint policies limit what principals can do through the endpoint, such as only allowing company buckets.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not encrypt, accelerate, or replicate.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A three-tier application uses an Application Load Balancer, EC2 Auto Scaling, and Aurora. During a recent outage, the database ran out of connections when the web tier scaled out. What is the best fix?
options: Add Amazon RDS Proxy to pool and share database connections
Disable Auto Scaling on the web tier
Increase the Aurora instance size every time it happens
Remove health checks from the load balancer
questions.correct_rationale: RDS Proxy pools connections and reduces connection storms from scaling fleets or Lambda.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling scaling hurts availability, resizing treats symptoms, and removing health checks hides failures.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A company wants its application to degrade gracefully when a non-critical recommendation service is down. Which pattern fits best?
options: Retry the call forever until it succeeds
Make the main page wait for the recommendation service
Remove all monitoring from the dependency
A circuit breaker with a timeout and a fallback response, such as default recommendations
questions.correct_rationale: Circuit breakers stop calling a failing dependency and return fallbacks so the core experience continues.
questions.distractor_summary: Unlimited retries and blocking waits spread the failure, and removing monitoring hides it.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: Which Route 53 routing policy sends traffic to resources based on the lowest network latency for the user?
options: Weighted routing
Geolocation routing
Latency-based routing
Simple routing
questions.correct_rationale: Latency routing returns the record for the Region that gives the user the lowest latency.
questions.distractor_summary: Weighted splits by percentage, geolocation uses the user's location, and simple returns one record set.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Design a strategy to meet reliability requirements
questions.question: A batch pipeline must complete even if individual processing steps fail intermittently. Steps run on Lambda and ECS. What should orchestrate it?
options: A cron job that runs all steps without error handling
AWS Step Functions with retry and catch configurations for each step
One Lambda function that runs every step for up to 15 minutes
Manual reruns after checking logs
questions.correct_rationale: Step Functions coordinates steps with built-in retries, error handling, and state tracking.
questions.distractor_summary: Cron without error handling and single long functions are fragile, and manual reruns are slow.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: An e-commerce site's checkout API must respond in under 100 ms worldwide. The data is user-specific and changes often. Which design helps most?
options: Cache all checkout responses in CloudFront for one day
Deploy the API in several Regions with latency-based routing and a globally replicated database such as DynamoDB global tables
Use a single Region with a larger instance size
Store user data in S3 and scan it on each request
questions.correct_rationale: Serving dynamic, user-specific data from nearby Regions with replicated data reduces latency.
questions.distractor_summary: Long caching breaks per-user dynamic data, one Region keeps distant users slow, and scanning S3 is slow.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: A Lambda function has slow first requests after idle periods, and the business requires consistent latency for an API. What should be configured?
options: Provisioned concurrency on the function's alias
Reserved concurrency set to zero
A larger deployment package
A longer timeout
questions.correct_rationale: Provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialized so requests avoid cold starts.
questions.distractor_summary: Zero reserved concurrency stops invocations, bigger packages slow starts, and timeouts do not reduce latency.

questions.subdomain: 2.5 Design a solution to meet performance objectives
questions.question: Which storage option offers the highest IOPS for a single EC2 database instance that needs sustained sub-millisecond latency?
options: EBS st1 throughput-optimized HDD
EBS sc1 cold HDD
Amazon S3 Standard
EBS io2 Block Express volumes
questions.correct_rationale: io2 Block Express provides very high IOPS and low latency for demanding databases.
questions.distractor_summary: st1 and sc1 are HDD types for throughput or cold data, and S3 is object storage.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A machine learning team runs training jobs a few times a month on GPU instances, and jobs can checkpoint progress. What reduces cost most?
options: Run On-Demand GPU instances all month
Buy three-year Reserved Instances for GPUs
Use managed Spot training with checkpointing, for example in SageMaker AI
Use Dedicated Hosts for training
questions.correct_rationale: Spot capacity with checkpoints resumes after interruptions and cuts training costs significantly.
questions.distractor_summary: Always-on and long-term commitments do not fit occasional jobs, and Dedicated Hosts add cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A company's NAT gateway charges are high because instances download large amounts of data from Amazon S3 in the same Region. What is the most cost-effective fix?
options: Add more NAT gateways
Move instances to public subnets with public IPs
Add an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and route S3 traffic through it
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway endpoints for S3 have no hourly or data processing charge and bypass the NAT gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: More NAT gateways add cost, public subnets add exposure, and Transfer Acceleration increases cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: Which S3 storage class is suitable for re-creatable data accessed infrequently, at lower cost than Standard-IA, stored in a single Availability Zone?
options: S3 Standard
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Intelligent-Tiering archive tiers only
questions.correct_rationale: One Zone-IA is cheaper because it stores data in one AZ, so it suits data you can recreate.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard costs more, Deep Archive has hours-long retrieval, and Intelligent-Tiering automates tiering rather than single-AZ storage.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A company runs a containerized microservice fleet on ECS with steady load. It wants to cut compute cost without managing commitments per instance type. What should it buy?
options: Compute Savings Plans that cover Fargate and EC2 usage
EC2 Instance Savings Plans for one instance family only
Spot Instances for the entire steady fleet
Dedicated Instances
questions.correct_rationale: Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2 and Fargate regardless of instance family.
questions.distractor_summary: Instance Savings Plans are tied to a family, Spot interruptions do not suit all steady services, and Dedicated Instances cost more.

questions.subdomain: 2.6 Determine a cost optimization strategy to meet solution goals and objectives
questions.question: A SaaS company wants to show each tenant's infrastructure cost in a shared environment. Which approach is most practical?
options: Create one AWS account per API request
Divide the total bill equally among all tenants
Use AWS Artifact to calculate tenant costs
Tag tenant-specific resources and use metering, such as per-tenant usage metrics, to apportion shared costs
questions.correct_rationale: Combining tagged resources with usage-based allocation gives fair per-tenant cost estimates.
questions.distractor_summary: Account per request is impossible, equal splits are inaccurate, and Artifact does not calculate costs.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Determine a strategy to improve overall operational excellence
questions.question: Operators patch hundreds of EC2 instances manually each month, and patching is often late. What should the architect recommend?
options: Disable patching to avoid downtime
Patch only the instances that users complain about
Rebuild every instance manually each month
Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager with maintenance windows and patch baselines
questions.correct_rationale: Patch Manager automates scanning and installing patches on a schedule with compliance reporting.
questions.distractor_summary: Skipping or partial patching leaves risk, and manual rebuilds are slow.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Determine a strategy to improve overall operational excellence
questions.question: Configuration drift keeps appearing between environments created with CloudFormation because engineers make console changes. What improves operational excellence most?
options: Allow console changes but ask engineers to document them
Delete and recreate stacks every day
Enforce changes through pipelines, detect drift with CloudFormation drift detection and AWS Config, and restrict console write access
Turn off CloudFormation and manage everything manually
questions.correct_rationale: Pipelines plus detection and restricted write access keep environments matching their templates.
questions.distractor_summary: Documentation does not prevent drift, daily recreation is disruptive, and manual management increases drift.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Determine a strategy to improve overall operational excellence
questions.question: Engineers need shell access to private EC2 instances, but security wants no bastion hosts, no open SSH ports, and full session logging. What fits best?
options: A bastion host with SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with session logging to S3 or CloudWatch Logs
Public IPs on every instance
